summary: This proposed standard defines how to encapsulate SNMP packets in IPX, the transport used on Novell NetWare networks, so network management can work there.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines how to carry Simple Network Management Protocol messages over IPX. It is intended for environments without UDP transport, while the memo identifies UDP as the preferred mapping.

subtitle: How SNMP messages can be carried over IPX in Novell NetWare environments.

tldr.problem: Some Novell NetWare environments needed SNMP transport where UDP was not available.
tldr.mechanism: SNMP packets are sent over IPX with Packet Type 4 and assigned sockets for requests and traps.
tldr.outcome: The memo says UDP remains the preferred SNMP mapping. RFC 1420 obsoletes RFC 1298.

today: RFC 1420 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 1298. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 1420.

sections.title: Why Use SNMP over IPX
sections.content:
The Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is used to manage TCP/IP networks. This RFC describes mapping SNMP onto Internetwork Packet Exchange (IPX), the protocol used in Novell NetWare environments.

The memo says UDP is the preferred transport mapping for SNMP. This IPX mapping is intended for environments where UDP is unavailable, and does not suggest that a managed agent in a mixed environment must support multiple mappings.
sections.plainLanguage: SNMP can use IPX in environments where UDP is not available. The memo says UDP remains the preferred mapping.

sections.title: Packet Type, Sockets and Replies
sections.content:
SNMP packets sent over IPX always set the Packet Type field to 4, called a Packet Exchange Packet. GetRequest-PDU, GetNextRequest-PDU and SetRequest-PDU messages are received on socket 36879, hexadecimal 900F. Trap-PDU messages are received on socket 36880, hexadecimal 9010.

A GetResponse-PDU is addressed to the IPX address and socket from which its request originated.
sections.plainLanguage: SNMP requests and traps use different IPX sockets. A response goes back to the address and socket that sent the request.

sections.title: Traps and Message Size
sections.content:
For an SNMP trap sent over IPX, the agent-addr field contains the IP address 0.0.0.0. An SNMP manager may identify the source using information from the transport service.

SNMP does not require implementations to accept messages longer than 484 bytes. The RFC recommends supporting a maximum message size of 546 bytes, the IPX maximum and the maximum guaranteed to pass through IPX routers that do not fragment packets. Longer packets may be used when their maximum is known.
sections.plainLanguage: For an IPX trap, the packet's agent address is set to 0.0.0.0. The RFC recommends support for messages up to 546 bytes.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that it does not discuss security issues. It defines the SNMP-to-IPX mapping and does not provide security guidance for it.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo does not discuss security issues for this mapping.
